[[File:American Airlines Center 02.jpg|thumb|The Stars have played their home games at the American Airlines Center since 2001.]]
The [[Dallas Stars]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Dallas]]. They play in the [[Central Division (NHL)|Central Division]] of the [[Western Conference (NHL)|Western Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2009-01-01}}</ref> The team joined the NHL in 1967 as an [[expansion team]] as the [[Minnesota North Stars]], but moved to Dallas in 1993.<ref>{{cite book| last = Showers| first = Bob| year = 2007| title = Minnesota North Stars: History and Memories with Lou Nanne| publisher = Beaver's Pond Press| isbn = 978-1-59298-197-7}}</ref> The Stars won their first [[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championship]] in 1999.<ref name="history">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |title=Stanley Cup Champions and Finalists |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |accessdate=2009-01-01 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090629213230/http://www.nhl.com/cup/champs.html |archivedate=2009-06-29 }}</ref> Having first played at the [[Reunion Arena]], the Stars have played their home games at the [[American Airlines Center]] since 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.americanairlinescenter.com/teams/dallas_stars.php|title=Dallas Stars|publisher=[[American Airlines Center]]|accessdate=2009-01-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081219084726/http://www.americanairlinescenter.com/teams/dallas_stars.php|archivedate=2008-12-19}}</ref> The current head coach is [[Glen Gulutzan]], who was hired for his second tenure as head coach on July 1, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/glen-gulutzan-hired-as-dallas-stars-head-coach-replaces-pete-deboer |title=Gulutzan hired as Stars coach, replaces DeBoer |website=nhl.com |date=July 1, 2025 |access-date=July 1, 2025}}</ref>

There have been eight&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Stars' team. The team's first head coach was [[Bob Gainey]], who coached for four seasons. In the middle of the [[1995–96 NHL season|1995–96 season]], Gainey, who was then also the general manager for the Stars, fired himself as head coach and hired [[Ken Hitchcock]] to take over.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9E03E5DC1F39F937A15756C0A96E958260&n=Top/News/Sports/Hockey/National%20Hockey%20League/Dallas%20Stars|title=The Stanley Cup Playoffs; Not Just a Pretty Face|work=[[The New York Times]]|accessdate=2009-01-02 | first=Joe | last=Drape | date=1998-05-24}}</ref> Hitchcock is the team's all-time leader for the most regular-season games coached (585), the most regular-season game wins (319), the most regular-season [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] (718), the most playoff games coached (80), and the most playoff-game wins (47). Hitchcock is the only Stars coach to have won the [[Presidents' Trophy]], winning it in 1997–98 and 1998–99, the [[Clarence S. Campbell Bowl]], winning it in 1998–99 and 1999–2000, and the [[Stanley Cup]], winning it in the [[1999 Stanley Cup Finals]] against the [[Buffalo Sabres]].<ref name="pres">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/trophies/presidents.html |title=Presidents' Trophy |publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League |work=NHL.com |accessdate=2009-01-01 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091013061929/http://www.nhl.com/trophies/presidents.html |archivedate=2009-10-13 }}</ref><ref name="csc">{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/trophies/campbell.html|title=Clarence S. Campbell Bowl|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2009-01-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080723230820/http://www.nhl.com/trophies/campbell.html|archivedate=2008-07-23}}</ref><ref name="history"/> Hitchcock returned for one more season with the Stars in [[2017–18 NHL season|2017–18]]. None of the Stars coaches have been elected into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as a [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|title=List of honoured builders|publisher=[[Hockey Hall of Fame]]|accessdate=2009-01-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528120538/http://www.legendsofhockey.net:8080/LegendsOfHockey/jsp/LegendsMembersByYear.jsp?type=Builder|archivedate=2009-05-28}}</ref>

==Notes==
*{{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Stars. Thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
*{{note label|Note2|b|b}} Before the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|title=Official Rules|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2009-01-01|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511234846/http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|archivedate=2008-05-11}}</ref>
